dependency-analysis.title: Dependency analysis in Azure Migrate Discovery and assessment – Microsoft Learn
dependency-analysis.notes: Dependency analysis is a feature of Azure Migrate that identifies how discovered running servers depend on one another. It covers on-premises servers in VMware and Hyper-V, physical servers, and servers in other public clouds. Its purpose is to inspect network dependencies, group interdependent servers into applications, and find servers that have to be migrated together, so that no component is overlooked and outages after migration are avoided. Two options exist. The agentless option collects TCP connection data without installing agents on the servers. It relates source server, process and port to destination server, process and port as a logical dependency, and shows the result as a map view or a CSV export. The Azure Migrate appliance polls the connection data, processes it locally and forwards it to the service in periodic batches. The agent-based option builds on the Service Map solution in Azure Monitor and needs an agent on every source server. It is only available in the classic experience, is not supported in Azure Government, and no new servers can be added to it.

dev-containers.title: Set up Dev Containers on Windows – Microsoft Learn
dev-containers.notes: A dev container lets a Docker container serve as a complete development environment. It is described by a devcontainer.json file that lives in the project repository, usually inside a .devcontainer folder. The goal is that everyone who opens the project gets the same tools, extensions and settings, regardless of what is installed on their own machine. When a folder is reopened in the container, the image is built from that configuration. A configuration can be added to an existing project through a Visual Studio Code command, which asks for a base image such as Node.js, Python or Debian/Ubuntu, and a command exists to return to the local environment. The full option reference is the Dev Container Specification. On Windows the setup expects WSL 2, Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 based engine enabled, Visual Studio Code and the Dev Containers extension. Performance depends on where the project is stored: projects kept in the Windows file system are noticeably slower than those in the WSL 2 file system, and file changes may not be detected there. Docker Desktop must be running before VS Code is opened, and WSL integration must be enabled for the distribution in use.

dynamics-365-human-resources.title: Human Resources home page – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-human-resources.notes: Dynamics 365 Human Resources is a Microsoft application that connects people data with operations data. According to its documentation home page, it provides workforce insights for building data-driven employee experiences, with the stated aims of optimizing workforce costs and taking care of employees. The documentation groups its functionality into several areas. These include employee self service, personnel management covering personnel records, departments and positions, task management, and leave and absence. Further areas are recruiting, benefits and benefits management, compensation management, employee development in the sense of performance management, and learning with courses. A workflow system is also listed and points to the documentation of the shared Finance and operations platform. The page links to Dynamics 365 Finance as a related product and points to online training on Microsoft Learn. It is an entry and directory page, so it gives no licensing details, system requirements, concrete usage scenarios or limits; those would have to be taken from the linked topic pages.

dynamics-365-knowledge-management.title: Overview of knowledge management – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-knowledge-management.notes: Knowledge management is a part of Dynamics 365 Customer Service in which team members create, categorize, publish, analyze and share information through a knowledge base. The purpose is to help service agents find information for immediate problem resolution and to let customers solve issues themselves through search across channels, which is meant to lower handling time and ticket volume. Knowledge authors get a rich-text editor, review before publishing, templates with prefilled fields, major and minor versions, translations into several languages, and scheduled publishing and expiry. Administrators set up hierarchical categories, external search providers such as websites crawled through a sitemap, search logic and filters, and analytics. Agents search through Smart Assist or the knowledge search pane in the Copilot Service workspace and can rate articles. A search analytics dashboard helps reveal searches with poor or no results and therefore gaps in the content. A Copilot agent can use the knowledge to answer simple questions. Drafting knowledge from cases with Copilot is marked as a preview feature. The page gives no licensing details or numeric limits.

dynamics-365-remote-assist.title: Welcome to Dynamics 365 Remote Assist – Microsoft Learn
dynamics-365-remote-assist.notes: Dynamics 365 Remote Assist is an application that lets technicians collaborate across locations, designed for HoloLens 2. The page states that it is a communication tool and not a medical device. Typical uses are joint repair and maintenance with a live video call from the technician's point of view, remote inspections, and knowledge sharing through documented repairs. Features include a heads-up video call with voice control, spatial annotations from a remote expert that stay anchored in the room, display of reference material such as schematics from OneDrive, screen sharing, snapshots, and call recording. Customers and service providers can join through a click-to-join call. Integration with Dynamics 365 Field Service allows bookings to be viewed and call details and files to be attached to the work order, and Power Platform can process photo and video data. The remote person uses Microsoft Teams on a PC or mobile device. For a call with an external Teams user, one participant needs a Field Service, Guides or Remote Assist license. Limits: holographic content appears only within the HoloLens field of view, the mobile app has been retired, and Guides and Remote Assist are announced to become unavailable at the end of 2026.

electronic-invoicing.title: Electronic invoicing service overview – Microsoft Learn
electronic-invoicing.notes: The Electronic invoicing service is a highly scalable multitenant service for Dynamics 365 Finance and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. It handles configurable processing of electronic invoices and configurable exchange of electronic documents. Its processing and integration rules are fully configurable, and the logic runs outside Finance and Supply Chain Management, so country-specific requirements can be adopted faster and configurations adjusted without code changes. Setup is done with globalization features in the Globalization Studio workspace. Business data is transformed into XML, JSON, TXT or CSV by Electronic reporting format configurations. Documents can be submitted to external web services, including certificate handling with digital signatures such as XMLDSig, and the service interprets web service responses with configurable error handling. Documents can also be sent by email and stored in SharePoint, and incoming documents can be received through email and SharePoint and processed in the applications. Customers of Finance and Supply Chain Management can use it under the licensing terms of those applications. Limits: there is no on-premises deployment, and the scope for a given country can depend on the release phase.

federated-connectors.title: Federated connectors overview – Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors – Microsoft Learn
federated-connectors.notes: Federated Copilot connectors link Microsoft 365 Copilot to external data sources through the Model Context Protocol. Data is retrieved in real time and is not indexed in Microsoft 365, so it stays where it originated and the source system remains the system of record. Access runs under the identity and permissions of the signed-in user, who authenticates with their own credentials via OAuth 2.0. Where a connector offers the matching tools, Copilot can also create, change or delete data in the connected system for the user; such write actions need the user's approval, and read tools do not. Activity can be audited in Microsoft Purview. Admins manage connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and connectors are either published by Microsoft or submitted by partners and approved. Users need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Typical examples are summarizing open project issues, turning an email into an issue, or updating a CRM record. Limits: the Researcher agent only reads, the available actions depend on the tools the publisher exposes, and federation works per user, unlike synced connectors that work at organization level.

financial-dimensions.title: Financial dimensions and tags – Finance – Microsoft Learn
financial-dimensions.notes: Financial dimensions in Dynamics 365 Finance categorize financial transactions further. Their values become segments within a main account, which makes it possible to report by dimension, for example a profit and loss statement or a trial balance. Custom dimensions have values that are maintained manually and always apply across legal entities. Entity-backed dimensions take their values from a system entity such as projects, customers or stores; they can be shared or specific to a company and must be edited in the source entity rather than on the dimension values page. Legal entity overrides allow a dimension value or main account to be suspended for particular legal entities, to assign responsible people and to set validity periods. Dimension data validation checks whether an account combination or default dimension combination is structurally valid. Financial tags are an alternative to dimensions. Limits named on the page: custom dimension values have a maximum length, dimensions are not meant to represent the operational needs of legal entities, intercompany functions cover postings only, sales tax works with legal entities rather than dimensions, and some reports do not include dimensions. The page lists no licensing requirements.

flux-cd.title: Application deployments with GitOps (Flux v2) – Azure Arc – Microsoft Learn
flux-cd.notes: Flux is an open-source toolset that Azure uses for GitOps application deployments on AKS and on Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters. In the GitOps approach the desired cluster state is declared in files in Git repositories, such as YAML manifests, Helm charts and Kustomize files, and Kubernetes controllers in the cluster continuously reconcile the actual state with it. Supported sources include Git and Helm repositories, buckets and Azure Blob Storage. The default controllers are Source, Kustomize, Helm and Notification, with optional image automation and image reflector controllers. Azure adds a configuration agent and a configuration controller that transfer configurations from Azure into the cluster and report status back. Flux runs on the cluster and works purely pull-based, so neither the source repository nor other clusters need access to it. It can be rolled out at scale through Azure Policy and supports multi-tenancy and dependency control between deployments. Limits: Azure supports only part of the Flux parameters, changes apply only when the agent can reach Azure, and cross-namespace references are blocked while multi-tenancy is enforced. There is no extra Flux charge on AKS, while other Arc-connected distributions are billed per vCPU after a free allowance.

fuzzy-matching.title: Fuzzy merge – Power Query – Microsoft Learn
fuzzy-matching.notes: In Power Query, fuzzy merge applies approximate matching algorithms when columns of two tables are compared, so rows can be joined even if the values are not exactly equal. A typical case is free-text survey answers containing typos, singular and plural variants or differences in letter case. It is switched on with a checkbox at the bottom of the Merge dialog and uses the Jaccard similarity algorithm to measure how alike two values are. The options include a similarity threshold between zero and one, where one means an exact match, an ignore-case setting, combining text parts so that split words such as two fragments of a name can match, an option to show similarity scores, a maximum number of matches per input row, and an optional transformation table that maps chosen values explicitly, using From and To columns. The similarity score helps decide whether the threshold should be raised or lowered. Rows without a match stay empty. The page's example reduces nine different survey answers to four after tuning the settings. Fuzzy matching is supported only for merges on text columns. The page names no licensing requirements.

hnsw.title: Relevance in vector search – Azure AI Search – Microsoft Learn
hnsw.notes: HNSW, short for Hierarchical Navigable Small World, is an approximate nearest neighbor algorithm that Azure AI Search uses for vector search. It is tuned for high recall and low latency when the data distribution is unknown or changing, and it trades a little accuracy for speed and scalability. During indexing the vectors form a layered graph in which upper layers are coarse and lower layers are fine. Each node is linked to a number of near neighbors, and long-range links create shortcuts. A query starts at the top layer, moves down layer by layer using the configured distance metric, prunes unlikely candidates with a priority queue and refines the result on the lower layers until the requested number of neighbors is found. Configurable parameters include the neighbor count per node, the number of candidates considered while building connections, the queue length during search, and the metric, which can be cosine, dot product or Euclidean. All data points must sit in memory, which consumes the vector index size quota. Query vectors must come from the same embedding model as the indexed ones. Exhaustive KNN is available on HNSW fields but is compute-intensive and suited to small or medium datasets.

just-enough-administration.title: Just Enough Administration overview – PowerShell – Microsoft Learn
just-enough-administration.notes: Just Enough Administration (JEA) is a security technology that enables delegated administration for anything that can be managed with PowerShell. It follows the principle of least privilege: regular users run privileged actions through virtual accounts or group-managed service accounts, so fewer people need administrator rights on a machine. A configurable management endpoint exposes only the permitted cmdlets, functions and external commands, which limits what users can do. Transcripts and logs record which commands a user ran in a session, which makes activity traceable. Temporary privileged virtual accounts let users with non-admin credentials execute commands that would normally require admin rights. The page gives the example of DNS administrators on a domain controller: without JEA they would need membership in the Domain Admins group, while with JEA they receive only the commands they need, such as repairing the DNS cache or restarting the DNS server, and no access to Active Directory, file system browsing or risky scripts. Samples and a DSC resource are provided in a GitHub repository. The page points to a separate article for prerequisites and mentions no licensing or explicit limitations.
